tasks.title: Implement pure snapshot schema builders and writers in huntr_snapshot_schema.py
acceptance_criteria: Provides build_eligible_cache, build_repo_bounties, build_existing_submissions, and write_snapshots.
Round-trips successfully through unchanged loaders load_cache, load_repo_bounties, and load_existing_submissions.
Writes snapshot files with sorted keys and stable ordering to target directory.
Runs pytest tests/test_huntr_snapshot_schema_wired.py -q successfully without any failures.

spec.objective: Build pure, dependency-free snapshot builders and writers that assemble and write the exact JSON shapes required by unchanged cache loaders.
functional_requirements: build_eligible_cache(repos, fetched_at) returns dict conforming to huntr_eligible_cache.json shape with sorted repos list and ISO8601 fetched_at string.
build_repo_bounties(repo_records) returns dict conforming to huntr_repo_bounties.json shape.
build_existing_submissions(submission_records) returns dict conforming to huntr_existing_submissions.json shape.
write_snapshots(data_dir, eligible, bounties, submissions) writes three snapshot files using sorted keys and stable ordering.
Ensure compatibility with existing load_cache, load_repo_bounties, and load_existing_submissions in ngv2/huntr_cache_loader.py.
Ensure the module is pure and dependency-free, avoiding imports of ngv2/sourcing/huntr_client.py or any network/browser IO.
edge_cases: Empty repository, bounty, or submission input collections.
Duplicate and unsorted repository lists to check that sorting and deduplication works.
non_goals: Do not perform network or browser operations to fetch data.
Do not write integration tests that make external calls; integration testing is excluded.
spec.implementation_notes:
Implement using Python standard library json and pathlib. Ensure json.dump uses sort_keys=True, indent=2, or whatever format matches the unchanged loaders' byte-exact requirements.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.


# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/test_huntr_snapshot_schema_wired.py
```python
"""RED oracle: ngv2/sourcing/huntr_snapshot_schema.py — pure builders +
deterministic writers for the three huntr snapshot JSON files.

Contract (from brief_hooks_sourcing-schema-and-parser):
    build_eligible_cache(repos: list[str], fetched_at: str) -> dict
    build_repo_bounties(repo_records: dict) -> dict
    build_existing_submissions(submission_records: dict) -> dict
    write_snapshots(data_dir: str, eligible: dict, bounties: dict, submissions: dict) -> None

Output shapes are EXACTLY what the unchanged loaders consume:
    huntr_eligible_cache.json      = {"repos": [sorted "owner/repo"], "fetched_at": iso8601}
    huntr_repo_bounties.json       = {"repos": {"owner/repo": {eligible, tier,
                                      observed_payouts{critical,high,medium,low},
                                      max_paid, total_advisories, submissions, pool_note}}}
    huntr_existing_submissions.json = {"owner/repo": {"status": int, "count": int,
                                       "titles": [str, ...]}}

``repo_records`` / ``submission_records`` are mappings of "owner/repo" to the
already-shaped per-repo record dicts shown above. Writers are deterministic
(byte-identical on identical input, sorted keys). Pure stdlib, no network.
The round-trip proof: the unchanged ngv2.huntr_cache_loader / check_eligible /
parse_bounties consume the written files without error.
"""
import json

from ngv2.sourcing.huntr_snapshot_schema import (
    build_eligible_cache,
    build_existing_submissions,
    build_repo_bounties,
    write_snapshots,
)
from ngv2.huntr_cache_loader import (
    ELIGIBLE_CACHE_FILE,
    EXISTING_SUBMISSIONS_FILE,
    REPO_BOUNTIES_FILE,
    load_cache,
    load_existing_submissions,
    load_repo_bounties,
)
from ngv2.huntr_data import parse_bounties, parse_existing_submissions
from ngv2.huntr_eligible_cache import check_eligible

FETCHED_AT = "2026-06-12T00:00:00+00:00"

RECORD = {
    "eligible": True,
    "tier": "B",
    "observed_payouts": {"critical": 1200, "high": 600, "medium": 100, "low": 15},
    "max_paid": 1200,
    "total_advisories": 28,
    "submissions": 28,
    "pool_note": "Active, well-funded program",
}


def test_build_eligible_cache_shape_and_sorting():
    out = build_eligible_cache(["b/y", "a/x", "b/y"], FETCHED_AT)
    assert out["fetched_at"] == FETCHED_AT
    assert out["repos"] == sorted(set(out["repos"]))
    assert "a/x" in out["repos"] and "b/y" in out["repos"]


def test_build_repo_bounties_shape():
    out = build_repo_bounties({"alpha/one": dict(RECORD)})
    assert set(out) >= {"repos"}
    rec = out["repos"]["alpha/one"]
    for key in (
        "eligible",
        "tier",
        "observed_payouts",
        "max_paid",
        "total_advisories",
        "submissions",
        "pool_note",
    ):
        assert key in rec
    assert set(rec["observed_payouts"]) >= {"critical", "high", "medium", "low"}


def test_build_existing_submissions_shape():
    out = build_existing_submissions(
        {"alpha/one": {"status": 200, "count": 2, "titles": ["t1", "t2"]}}
    )
    assert out["alpha/one"]["status"] == 200
    assert out["alpha/one"]["count"] == 2
    assert out["alpha/one"]["titles"] == ["t1", "t2"]


def test_write_snapshots_round_trips_into_unchanged_loaders(tmp_path):
    eligible = build_eligible_cache(["alpha/one", "beta/two"], FETCHED_AT)
    bounties = build_repo_bounties({"alpha/one": dict(RECORD)})
    submissions = build_existing_submissions(
        {"alpha/one": {"status": 200, "count": 1, "titles": ["OS Command Injection in runner"]}}
    )
    write_snapshots(str(tmp_path), eligible, bounties, submissions)

    for name in (ELIGIBLE_CACHE_FILE, REPO_BOUNTIES_FILE, EXISTING_SUBMISSIONS_FILE):
        assert (tmp_path / name).is_file()

    cache = load_cache(tmp_path)
    assert cache is not None and cache["fetched_at"] == FETCHED_AT

    verdict = check_eligible("alpha/one", load_cache=lambda: load_cache(tmp_path))
    assert verdict["eligible"] is True
    assert verdict["cache_date"] == FETCHED_AT

    parsed = parse_bounties(load_repo_bounties(tmp_path))
    assert [b.repo for b in parsed] == ["alpha/one"]
    assert parsed[0].eligible is True and parsed[0].max_paid == 1200

    subs = parse_existing_submissions(load_existing_submissions(tmp_path))
    assert subs == {"alpha/one": ["OS Command Injection in runner"]}


# edge_case: writers are deterministic — identical input => byte-identical files
def test_write_snapshots_is_deterministic(tmp_path):
    a, b = tmp_path / "a", tmp_path / "b"
    a.mkdir()
    b.mkdir()
    eligible = build_eligible_cache(["z/z", "a/a"], FETCHED_AT)
    bounties = build_repo_bounties({"z/z": dict(RECORD), "a/a": dict(RECORD)})
    submissions = build_existing_submissions({"a/a": {"status": 200, "count": 0, "titles": []}})
    write_snapshots(str(a), eligible, bounties, submissions)
    write_snapshots(str(b), eligible, bounties, submissions)
    for name in (ELIGIBLE_CACHE_FILE, REPO_BOUNTIES_FILE, EXISTING_SUBMISSIONS_FILE):
        assert (a / name).read_bytes() == (b / name).read_bytes()


# edge_case: empty inputs still produce loader-consumable files (never raise)
def test_empty_inputs_still_loader_consumable(tmp_path):
    write_snapshots(
        str(tmp_path),
        build_eligible_cache([], FETCHED_AT),
        build_repo_bounties({}),
        build_existing_submissions({}),
    )
    cache = load_cache(tmp_path)
    assert cache is not None and cache["repos"] == []
    assert parse_bounties(load_repo_bounties(tmp_path)) == []
    assert parse_existing_submissions(load_existing_submissions(tmp_path)) == {}
    # files are valid JSON
    for name in (ELIGIBLE_CACHE_FILE, REPO_BOUNTIES_FILE, EXISTING_SUBMISSIONS_FILE):
        json.loads((tmp_path / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

```

tasks.title: Implement React-Server-Component flight payload extractor in huntr_page_parser.py
acceptance_criteria: Correctly handles both HTML-wrapped push chunks and raw RSC flight streams.
Accurately handles length-prefixed text rows (e.g. containing newlines) via scan-decoders.
Passes all performance requirements without catastrophic regex backtracking on large real fixtures.

spec.objective: Build pure React-Server-Component (RSC) flight payload extractor over injected HTML strings for hacktivity feeds, per-repo disclosures, and bounty indexes.
functional_requirements: parse_hacktivity(html) extracts feed items containing id, title, createdAt, patch_commit_sha, status, cve_id, cvss, cwe{id,description}, repository{owner,name,language}, disclosure{amount}, and maintainer triage.
parse_repo_page(html) extracts repository page disclosures and maintainer rationales (like #score|0|awarded, #self_closedduplicate, and free-text).
parse_bounties_index(html) extracts sorted, de-duplicated, and lowercased owner/name strings from server-rendered anchor tags.
Support parsing both HTML-wrapped self.__next_f.push chunks and bare raw RSC flight streams.
Handle length-prefixed text rows (<id>:T<hexlen>,<raw>) with newlines correctly by avoiding naive line-splitting.
Extract payload fixtures efficiently (up to 430KB) under tests/fixtures/huntr/ without causing catastrophic regex backtracking.
edge_cases: Bare raw RSC flight streams containing length-prefixed text rows with newlines inside raw content.
Bounty index anchor links with mixed casings and duplicate URLs that must be lowercased, sorted, and deduplicated.
non_goals: Do not perform network I/O or browser automation to download page HTML.
Do not perform full end-to-end integration tests requiring external servers; integration is a non-goal.
